text: Kokernag (Urdu pronunciation: [koːkərnɑːɡ]; Kashmiri pronunciation: [kɔkarnaːɡ]) is a sub-district, town, and notified area committee located in the Breng Valley, also known as the Golden Crown of Kashmir, within the Anantnag district of the Indian union territory of Jammu and Kashmir. It is renowned for its botanical gardens, pristine freshwater springs, and rainbow trout farm and lies 25.3 km from Anantnag District via NH244. It is one of the most popular weekend getaways from the state capital, Srinagar. The etymology of the name 'Kokernag' (Kashmiri: کۄکرناگ) is disputed, with no conclusive historical proof; one theory suggests it comes from 'koker' (Kashmiri for chicken) and 'nag' (Sanskrit for springs), as the springs emerge from a hillside resembling a hen’s claw-foot. Another theory interprets 'koker' as 'fowl' and 'nag' as 'serpent'. A third theory proposes that 'Kokernag' derives from 'Koh' (mountain), 'kan' (from or under), and 'nag' (spring). The place is also known as Breng Kokernag, a name given by poet and scholar Shiekh ul Alam, who stated "kokernag breng chu sunsund preng," meaning "Kokernag is crown of gold." Kokernag is mentioned in Ain Akbari, which notes that its water satisfies hunger and thirst and acts as a remedy for indigestion. Situated at an altitude of approximately 2,000 meters above sea level, Kokernag is surrounded by towns including Wangam, Devalgam, Hangalgund, Nagam, Sagam, Zalengam, Magam, and Soaf Shali. The Kokernag trout farm covers a total area of about 400 kanals, of which 129 kanals are allocated for gardens and other purposes. The area is famous for its trout streams and is home to the largest freshwater spring in Kashmir. The Trout Fish Farming Project Kokernag, established in 1984 with assistance from the European Economic Community, functions as the mother unit for producing quality Rainbow Trout and Brown Trout. Under its extension program, 59 trout rearing units/hatcheries have been set up across nearly all districts of the state, including Leh and Kargil, with more units being developed. Trout is readily available to the public at all rearing units, including a special sale outlet at Gagribal. A rural mart has been established in Kokernag by NABARD to promote and market handicrafts made by local women self-help groups. According to the 2011 India census, Kokernag had a population of 6,553, with males making up 68% and females 32% of the population. The average literacy rate is 63%, higher than the national average of 59.5%, with male literacy at 77% and female literacy at 33%. Nine percent of the population is under six years of age. Kokernag is located about 25 km from Anantnag on the right side of NH244, and the easiest way to reach it is by hiring a Sumo in Anantnag or taking a local bus, which takes approximately one hour. The nearest railway station is Anantnag railway station on the 119 km-long Kashmir Railway line from Baramulla to Banihal, located 30 km away. The nearest airport is Srinagar International Airport, situated 85 kilometers from Kokernag.
